subject: Clark's nutcracker
title: This Bird Buries 30,000 Seeds and Finds Them Under Snow

scenes.text: A bird buries thirty thousand seeds. It never writes down where.
A Clark's nutcracker hides pine seeds in more than two thousand five hundred separate spots.
Then winter buries everything under snow. Months later, it flies straight to the right spot and digs.
It has no map. It remembers where each seed sits compared to rocks and trees.
In one experiment, scientists moved the landmarks about eight inches. The birds dug in the wrong place.
Some caches get found nine months later. That is a memory built for winter.

description:
A Clark's nutcracker buries around thirty thousand pine seeds and finds them again under snow.
It does it with spatial memory, using landmarks, and can recover seeds up to nine months later.
Could you find one thing you hid last winter? Tell us below.
